> 否。否之匪人，不利君子貞，大往小來。

The twelfth hexagram is the mirror of the eleventh, and its name is one of the plainest words in the language.

## 否 means "not"

說文: 否，不也。從口，不聲.

It is the differentiated form of 不 — the same word, given a mouth.

Two readings must be kept apart: as the general negative, fǒu; as the name of this hexagram, pǐ (釋文: 否，備鄙反), where the sense is closed up, blocked.

So 否's original sense is not "evil." It is "not." First a "is-not," and only then a "does not get through."

That order matters, because it keeps the hexagram from becoming a moral verdict about bad people. What 否 describes is a condition in which the passage is shut, and the people on either side of the shut passage are not the cause.

## 匪人 — not the right time for the right person

匪 is 非. 匪人 is "not the person," in the sense of: this is not a ground on which the upright can operate.

The judgement does not say the upright are wrong. It says that in a closed time, the same conduct that worked in 泰 cannot be deployed — 不利君子貞.

Which is the hardest part of the hexagram for a reader who wants an ethics: there is a season when holding the standard means not acting on it.

## 大往小來

Exactly inverted from 泰: yang recedes outward, yin settles inward.

Correct influence dissipates; private interest takes up the interior.

## 包承 and 包羞

Both take 包 — to contain, to hold in.

But the objects differ:

包承 is containing someone's compliance — bearing with a subordinate who bends and defers.
包羞 is containing one's own shame — holding in a humiliation one knows to be a humiliation, and not letting it out.

The 象's comment on 包羞 is three characters: 位不當也. Not that it is wrong to hold it in, but that holding it in is what an improper position produces. The line is a diagnosis of a place, not of a person.

## 疇離祉

疇: class, kind. 離 here is read lì — to attach, to adhere (not "to depart," and not the hexagram 離).

祉: blessing.

So: those of the same kind attach to the charge and share the blessing together.

Which is 否's only consolation. In a closed time, like finds like — not to build a faction, but so that the standard is kept somewhere while it cannot be kept publicly.

## 休否

說文: 休，息止也.

九五 休否: to bring the closure to rest, to arrest it before it spreads further.

And the same line adds the most quoted phrase in the hexagram: 其亡其亡，繫于苞桑.

苞 is growing in a clump. A clump of mulberry has roots knotted deep.

So the vigilance is tied to something that can hold it. The sentence is not "be careful." It is: find the deep roots, and tie your fear there.

## 傾否

The top line: 傾否，先否後喜.

To overturn the closure — and the 象 says 否終則傾: when the closure reaches its end, it tips by itself.

Not broken by force. The condition exhausts itself.

Which is a strange and useful statement: the end of a closed time is not won, it is reached. What the person does at that point is not push but stand where the tipping will land.

## The test

Take a situation where you are right and cannot get through. Ask which of the two things you are doing: 包承 (bearing with someone else's compliance) or 包羞 (bearing your own shame). They look identical from outside and have different futures. The first is a relation; the second is a position that is not yours yet.
